job.title: Manager Engineering Services
job.description:
Manager Engineering Services
Isaac Regional Council | Isaac Region QLD | Infrastructure Leadership | Circa $230k to $250 TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Isaac Regional Council to recruit a Manager Engineering Services—an expanded leadership opportunity bringing together infrastructure planning, capital delivery and technical services across a diverse regional portfolio.
  
You will lead and develop the people who plan, design and support the delivery of infrastructure for Isaac’s communities. With the team’s scope recently expanded, this is an opportunity to establish clear priorities, strengthen capability and shape how the function works within Council’s Infrastructure Services Directorate.
  
Council is seeking a leader who combines technical credibility with the ability to motivate people, negotiate competing priorities and turn plans into practical outcomes. Your influence will extend across transport, water and wastewater projects, asset renewals, road access and infrastructure agreements with industry.
  
The Role
  
You will oversee infrastructure planning, design coordination and capital delivery, working closely with other managers and asset owners to develop balanced investment programs that respond to community needs and Council priorities.
  
An early focus will be bringing the expanded team together, clarifying responsibilities and supporting recruitment and development in key positions while maintaining momentum across the capital program. Most detailed design is outsourced, so your ability to scope requirements, manage consultants and assess technical quality will be central to success.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing engineering and technical staff, building a collaborative and performance-focused culture
  • Developing 5-, 10- and 20-year infrastructure priorities and capital works programs across Council portfolios
  • Coordinating infrastructure planning, asset renewals and delivery of transport and water-related capital projects
  • Managing external design consultants, technical specifications, construction standards and engineering reports
  • Overseeing heavy vehicle access approvals, third-party road corridor access and infrastructure agreements with mining companies and developers
  • Providing engineering input into development and operational works assessments in collaboration with Council’s planning teams
  • Coordinating bridge inspection requirements and oversight of Council aerodromes and aircraft landing areas
  • Identifying grant opportunities and preparing funding submissions for infrastructure investment
  • Building trusted relationships with government agencies, industry, contractors, elected representatives and communities
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil infrastructure leader who can provide direction to a broad team, develop emerging talent and balance engineering requirements with commercial, community and political considerations. You bring sound judgement, a pragmatic approach and the confidence to negotiate constructively with industry and government stakeholders.
  
You will bring:
  • Proven people leadership, with experience managing department functions, coaching staff and building capability
  • At least 10 years’ demonstrated civil engineering experience, or significant other relevant experience
  • Strong infrastructure planning, asset management and capital program development capability
  • Experience leading design and technical services across roads, drainage, traffic or related infrastructure
  • The ability to manage consultants and contractors, interpret technical designs and deliver value for money
  • Knowledge of civil construction and maintenance, relevant Queensland requirements and TMR specifications
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills, including managing competing priorities
  • Proficiency in Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Project
  • A Construction White Card and valid driver licence
  
A Civil Engineering degree, or a similar engineering degree with relevant civil experience, is desirable. RPEQ certification and postgraduate management qualifications are also highly regarded.
  
Local government experience will be an advantage, particularly where you understand capital planning, approvals and public sector decision-making. Council also welcomes leaders from consulting, infrastructure and other relevant sectors who can demonstrate strong people leadership and adapt to the local government environment. Specialist aviation experience is not a prerequisite; the role is supported by staff with operational aerodrome expertise.
  
Why Join Isaac Regional Council
  
Isaac is a region that feeds, powers and builds communities. This role offers the opportunity to connect significant infrastructure investment with the everyday needs of regional communities, while working with industry and government on the infrastructure that supports the region’s future.
  
  • Base salary of $170,000–$190,000, with flexibility considered for an exceptional candidate
  • Council housing and vehicle arrangements, or allowances in lieu, subject to agreed terms
  • Relocation assistance to support your move to the region
  • An expanded leadership remit with influence over infrastructure planning and capital delivery
  • The opportunity to develop your team, shape ways of working and make a visible contribution to community services
Council’s preference is for the successful candidate to be based within the Isaac region, providing visible leadership and becoming part of the communities they serve.

job.title: People & Culture Business Partner
job.description:
About Frankston City Council
Frankston City Council is an active local government organisation serving a diverse and growing community across Melbourne’s south-east. Council is committed to delivering high quality services and creating a positive experience for its employees, residents and broader community.

The People & Culture team plays an important role in supporting Council’s leaders to build capable, engaged and high-performing teams. With a focus on trusted partnerships, practical advice and continuous improvement, the team works across Council to support the full employee lifecycle and deliver people outcomes aligned to Council’s priorities.


About the Role
The People & Culture Business Partner is a key role within Frankston City Council’s People & Culture team, partnering with leaders across Council to provide strategic and operational HR advice across the full employee lifecycle.

Reporting to the Coordinator Business Partnering, you will work closely with Managers, Directors and people leaders across Council to provide practical, contemporary HR advice across employee relations, performance management, organisational change, workforce planning, employment matters and the interpretation of Council’s Enterprise Agreement and relevant legislation.

This is a genuine HR generalist Business Partner role, with a strong focus on employee relations. You will manage and advise on a range of complex people matters, including performance management, grievances, workplace disputes, misconduct and complaints relating to discrimination, harassment and bullying.

You will be trusted to lead investigations and provide sound advice to leaders, ensuring matters are managed effectively, fairly and in line with Council’s policies, legislation and employment framework.

You will also support organisational change and consultation processes, contribute to People & Culture projects and initiatives, and use people data and insights to inform decision making and workforce planning. The role provides the opportunity to work across a broad range of HR matters rather than being limited to one specialist area.

You will join a collaborative Business Partnering team, within a broader People & Culture function of approximately 20 professionals. Council is looking for someone who is proactive, energetic and willing to roll up their sleeves and contribute wherever needed.


About You
An experienced HR professional with strong generalist HR capability and a proven ability to partner with leaders and provide practical, strategic advice across the employee lifecycle.

Strong employee relations experience will be important, particularly across performance management, workplace investigations and complex employee matters. The ability to confidently interpret employment legislation, Enterprise Agreements, policies and procedures, and translate these into clear, practical advice for leaders.

Strong stakeholder management skills are equally important. This role will suit someone who enjoys working closely with leaders at all levels, influencing outcomes and building trusted partnerships, while also having the confidence to challenge, advise and provide an alternative perspective when required.

A proactive and solutions focused approach, together with the ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities, will be essential. This is a broad HR role within a fast moving environment, respond confidently to a range of people matters and step in to support the broader team when needed.

Experience within a large, complex or fast paced organisation will be highly regarded. Previous Local Government experience is desirable, however Council is open to strong HR Business Partners from other large, unionised environments who can demonstrate relevant transferable experience.
  
This role would strongly suit:
  • An experienced HR Business Partner with strong generalist HR and employee relations experience
  • A People & Culture professional looking to step into a genuine partnering role with broad exposure across the employee lifecycle
  • A Business Partner or experienced Advisor who enjoys working closely with leaders, providing practical advice and helping resolve complex people matters
  • An experienced HR professional from Local Government, health, education, NFP or another large unionised organisation looking to bring their skills into a diverse Council environment
A relevant qualification in Human Resources or a related discipline is desirable, together with demonstrated ER experience, strong knowledge of employment law and contemporary HR practices. Experience working within a large, complex or fast-paced organisation will be highly regarded.


The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to join Frankston City Council at an exciting time and contribute to a growing People & Culture function.

This role will have the opportunity to build strong relationships across Council and provide meaningful support to leaders as the organisation continues to evolve.

You will join an experienced and collaborative P&C team where your HR expertise, proactive approach and ability to build trusted relationships will be valued.

Frankston City Council also offers a range of benefits designed to support flexibility, wellbeing and work life balance, including:
  • Additional paid leave between the Christmas and New Year period, on top of four weeks annual leave
  • Monthly RDO arrangements
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
  • Purchased leave
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Free onsite parking at the Civic Centre
  • Salary sacrifice gym membership at Peninsula Aquatic Recreation Centre
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Social Club and employee activities
  • Professional and career development opportunities
Salary: Band 6, $100,338 + superannuation

Application Process

Public Sector People are partnering exclusively with Frankston City Council on this appointment. All applications and enquiries will be managed by Public Sector People.

Hobsons Bay City Council serves a diverse and established municipality in Melbourne’s inner west, encompassing residential neighbourhoods, established activity centres, industrial precincts and a range of community and Council assets.

Council’s building services function plays an important role in protecting community safety, responding to illegal building work and ensuring statutory obligations under the Building Act and Regulations are effectively delivered.

The service has recently undergone a realignment that has introduced clearer leadership across its two operational streams. A Deputy Municipal Building Surveyor now leads the building surveying function, while a Senior Building Surveyor oversees building site compliance and associated local laws activity.
This provides the incoming Municipal Building Surveyor with an experienced and stable team, a capable leadership structure and a strong platform from which to consolidate recent improvements and guide the future direction of the service.

Hobsons Bay is a values-led organisation committed to providing practical, responsive and community-focused services.

About the Role

The Municipal Building Surveyor is responsible for administering Council’s statutory building functions and providing leadership, technical oversight and strategic direction to an established team of approximately 11 staff.

The team operates across two complementary streams. The building surveying function includes the Deputy Municipal Building Surveyor, building surveyors, inspection, technical and administrative support.
